points.title: 早年教育与成长
points.description: 塞缪尔·贝克特出生于都柏林一个新教中产阶级家庭，在圣三一学院接受教育。他主修法语和意大利语，对文学和哲学产生浓厚兴趣。这一时期，他开始接触詹姆斯·乔伊斯的作品，并成为其助手，协助研究《芬尼根的守灵夜》。贝克特在都柏林的早期生活为他后来的文学创作奠定了基础，特别是他对语言、存在主义和荒诞主义的初步探索。
points.descriptionEn: Samuel Beckett was born into a Protestant middle-class family in Dublin and educated at Trinity College. He majored in French and Italian, developing a keen interest in literature and philosophy. During this period, he began to engage with the works of James Joyce and became his assistant, helping with research on 'Finnegans Wake'. Beckett's early life in Dublin laid the foundation for his later literary work, particularly his initial explorations into language, existentialism, and absurdism.

points.title: 巴黎求学与文学启蒙
points.description: 贝克特以法语讲师身份前往巴黎高等师范学院，这是他人生的重要转折点。在巴黎，他不仅深化了与乔伊斯的友谊，还结识了包括普鲁斯特、艾略特在内的多位文学大师。这一时期，他开始创作自己的诗歌和短篇小说，同时深入研究哲学，尤其是笛卡尔和柏格森的思想。巴黎的多元文化环境和文学氛围极大地拓展了他的视野，促使他形成了独特的文学风格和哲学思考。
points.descriptionEn: Beckett moved to Paris as a lecturer of French at the École Normale Supérieure, marking a significant turning point in his life. In Paris, he not only deepened his friendship with Joyce but also met numerous literary masters including Proust and Eliot. During this period, he began writing his own poetry and short stories while delving into philosophy, particularly the works of Descartes and Bergson. The multicultural environment and literary atmosphere of Paris greatly expanded his horizons, prompting the formation of his unique literary style and philosophical thinking.

points.title: 动荡岁月与创作低谷
points.description: 贝克特返回爱尔兰后在都柏林三一学院任教，但因与校方不和而辞职。他随后游历欧洲多地，包括伦敦和柏林，期间经历了严重的个人危机和创作瓶颈。这一时期，他经历了母亲的去世和与女友关系的破裂，导致他陷入深度抑郁。然而，正是这段低谷期促使他重新审视自己的创作方向，开始探索更简约、更具实验性的表达方式，为后来的代表作《等待戈多》奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: Beckett returned to Ireland and taught at Trinity College Dublin but resigned due to conflicts with the administration. He then traveled extensively across Europe, including London and Berlin, experiencing a severe personal crisis and creative block. During this period, he faced his mother's death and the breakdown of his relationship with his girlfriend, leading to deep depression. However, this low period prompted him to re-examine his creative direction, beginning to explore more minimalist and experimental forms of expression, laying the foundation for his later masterpiece 'Waiting for Godot'.

points.title: 创作巅峰与成名作
points.description: 二战后贝克特重返巴黎，并在此度过了余生的大部分时间。1953年，他的代表作《等待戈多》在巴黎首演，这部荒诞派戏剧的巨大成功使他一举成名。随后，他创作了一系列重要作品，包括《终局》、《克拉普的最后一盘录音带》等戏剧作品，以及小说《莫菲》、《马龙之死》等。这一时期，贝克特形成了独特的'极简主义'风格，通过简约的语言和荒诞的情节探索人类存在的本质、孤独和绝望等主题，成为荒诞派戏剧的代表人物。
points.descriptionEn: After World War II, Beckett returned to Paris, where he would spend most of the rest of his life. In 1953, his masterpiece 'Waiting for Godot' premiered in Paris, achieving enormous success and catapulting him to fame. Subsequently, he created a series of important works including the plays 'Endgame', 'Krapp's Last Tape', and novels 'Murphy', 'Malone Dies', among others. During this period, Beckett developed his distinctive minimalist style, exploring themes of human existence, loneliness, and despair through concise language and absurd plots, becoming a leading figure in the Theatre of the Absurd.

points.title: 晚年创作与诺贝尔奖
points.description: 贝克特晚年继续创作，作品风格更加简约和实验性，包括《呼吸》、《电影》等。1969年，他因'以新的小说和戏剧形式，使现代人从贫困的境地中得到振奋'而获得诺贝尔文学奖，成为世界文学界的重要人物。尽管声名显赫，贝克特仍保持低调的生活方式，拒绝公开露面和采访。他晚年主要用法语创作，然后自己翻译成英语，体现了双语创作的独特性。贝克特于1989年在巴黎逝世，但他的作品对现代戏剧和文学的影响持续至今，被视为20世纪最重要的作家之一。
points.descriptionEn: In his later years, Beckett continued to write with increasingly minimalist and experimental works, including 'Breath' and 'Film'. In 1969, he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature 'for his writing, which—in new forms for the novel and drama—in the destitution of modern man uplifts his mind'. Despite his fame, Beckett maintained a low-profile lifestyle, avoiding public appearances and interviews. He primarily wrote in French and then translated his works into English himself, reflecting his unique bilingual creativity. Beckett died in Paris in 1989, but his influence on modern theater and literature continues to this day, establishing him as one of the most important writers of the 20th century.

supporter.zh: 贝克特被誉为现代主义文学的巨匠，他的作品深刻揭示了人类存在的荒诞性和孤独感。支持者认为，通过极简主义的表现形式，贝克特成功捕捉了现代人精神世界的困境，为后现代文学开辟了新路径。他的《等待戈多》等作品不仅是戏剧史上的里程碑，更是对人类处境的哲学思考，影响了无数后来的作家和艺术家。贝克特坚持用艺术探索人类存在的本质，这种执着追求使他成为20世纪最具影响力的作家之一。
supporter.en: Beckett is hailed as a giant of modernist literature, whose works profoundly reveal the absurdity and loneliness of human existence. Supporters argue that through minimalist expression, Beckett successfully captured the spiritual predicament of modern people,开辟ing new paths for postmodern literature. His works like 'Waiting for Godot' are not only milestones in theater history but also philosophical reflections on the human condition, influencing countless later writers and artists. Beckett's persistent pursuit of exploring the essence of human existence through art has established him as one of the most influential writers of the 20th century.

critic.zh: 批评者认为贝克特的作品过于悲观和虚无，缺乏积极的社会意义。他们指出，贝克特笔下的人物往往处于被动和绝望的状态，无法提供任何解决问题的方案。此外，他的极简主义风格有时被批评为晦涩难懂，远离普通读者的理解范围。一些评论家还质疑贝克特对传统叙事结构的彻底颠覆是否真的有助于文学发展，还是仅仅是一种形式上的实验。这些批评者认为，贝克特虽然技巧高超，但其作品缺乏人文关怀和社会责任感。
critic.en: Critics argue that Beckett's works are excessively pessimistic and nihilistic, lacking positive social significance. They point out that characters in Beckett's plays are often in passive and desperate states, unable to offer any solutions to problems. Additionally, his minimalist style is sometimes criticized as obscure and difficult for ordinary readers to understand. Some commentators also question whether Beckett's complete subversion of traditional narrative structures truly contributes to literary development or is merely formal experimentation. These critics believe that while Beckett is highly skilled, his works lack humanistic concern and social responsibility.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，贝克特被定义为荒诞派戏剧的代表人物和现代主义文学的重要先驱。他的作品超越了单纯的文学范畴，成为哲学和文化现象，影响了从戏剧到电影、从文学到艺术等多个领域。贝克特的双语创作背景使他成为连接英语和法语文学传统的桥梁，其作品被翻译成数十种语言，在全球范围内广泛传播。在流行文化中，'等待戈多'已成为一个文化符号，代表着无意义的等待和存在的荒诞性。贝克特的艺术成就和思想深度使他成为20世纪不可忽视的文化现象。
objective.en: In academic and popular culture, Beckett is defined as a representative of the Theatre of the Absurd and an important pioneer of modernist literature. His works transcend the realm of mere literature, becoming philosophical and cultural phenomena that have influenced multiple fields from theater to film, and from literature to art. Beckett's bilingual background made him a bridge between English and French literary traditions, and his works have been translated into dozens of languages, enjoying widespread dissemination globally. In popular culture, 'Waiting for Godot' has become a cultural symbol representing meaningless waiting and the absurdity of existence. Beckett's artistic achievements and intellectual depth have established him as an indispensable cultural phenomenon of the 20th century.

self.zh: 尝试失败，再尝试失败，以更好的失败尝试。
self.en: Try again. Fail again. Fail better.

others.zh: 贝克特是唯一一位能够同时用英语和法语写作，且两种语言都达到同等高度的作家。他的作品是对人类处境最深刻的探索之一。
others.en: Beckett is the only writer who could write equally well in both English and French, reaching the same heights in both languages. His work is one of the most profound explorations of the human condition.
